source.title: Compute Optimal Inference and Provable Amortisation Gap in Sparse Autoencoders

record.tranche_reason: Tests the validity of feature explanations using automated prediction on held-out activating and non-activating examples, rather than measuring the claim’s stated neuron-pole audit shares.
record.gate_note: The study reports GPT-4o explanation-validation F1 results for GPT-2 feature models, which bear on V6 and V7. It does not report the Qwen3 pole shares, a cross-model or scale audit, InceptionV1 examples, or attribution-graph reconstruction results. Other results such as reconstruction loss, sparsity, and dead-neuron rates do not measure the versions’ explanation-validity claims.
record.test_reason: The study scores GPT-4o explanations of sparse-dictionary features (SAE, MLP encoder, LCA) trained on GPT-2 Small Layer 9 residual activations. It uses this only to compare its own encoders. It never explains or scores the model's own neurons, and its detection-style F1 is not activation simulation. So it does not bear on any version, all of which concern neurons. The main contribution is a theorem and synthetic experiments on the SAE amortisation gap.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly right. The authors' main conclusion is that linear-nonlinear SAE encoders provably have a non-zero amortisation gap, and that sparse coding and MLPs often outperform them on synthetic data. They also conclude that MLP-encoded GPT-2 features score higher on automated interpretability than SAE and LCA features. They say this refutes the assumption that simpler encoders are needed for interpretability, while noting the MLP–SAE gap needs investigation and LCA was likely undertrained.
record.recipe_differences: Uses an automated feature-interpreter and feature-scorer pipeline on SAE, MLP, and LCA features from GPT-2 Small Layer 9; it does not reproduce the Qwen3 neuron-pole audit. The interpretation prompt uses top activating examples and logit effects, and the validation step uses new activating and non-activating examples.
record.method_sensitivity: Explanation-validation F1 differs by encoding method: MLP is higher than SAE and LCA.

fits_no_version.finding: GPT-4o explanations of dictionary features for GPT-2 Small Layer 9 reach detection F1 of about 0.6 (SAE, LCA) and 0.83 (MLP encoder) on held-out activating and non-activating examples. MLP is significantly higher (Kruskal-Wallis H=1856.33, p<0.001).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Explanation validity of learned sparse-dictionary features, as judged by automated detection F1, depends on encoder architecture; more expressive encoders yield more interpretable features.

record.problems: The reported F1 distributions have no per-method uncertainty estimates or reported fraction above a defined quality threshold. The interpretability assessment uses GPT-4o for both explanation generation and validation, and covers only GPT-2 Small Layer 9 features. The authors note that LCA implementation and training may be suboptimal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results bearing on V1–V7 were left out. Other reported metrics, including reconstruction loss, mean L0, dead-neuron rates, and synthetic sparse-code MCC, do not directly measure the claim versions’ neuron-pole explanation-validity outcomes.

untested.parts: No test of whether explanations of model neurons drawn from activating examples fail to predict firing. Only dictionary features were evaluated.
No simulation-based scoring of neuron explanations, no share of neurons with good scores, and no comparison of explainer strengths.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the rows to V6 and V7, but these are SAE-style dictionary features, not neurons, and the scoring is detection rather than simulation. The reader's labels are dropped. Figure 7 shows means (0.63, 0.83, 0.61) with N=2500, whereas the text reports medians and 500 features per method. GPT-4o is used for both explanation generation and scoring.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B pole audit or shares of poles by number of jobs or understanding status.
No audit of neuron-pole job shares across language models, architectures, or parameter scales.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car example or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, or tool effects on interpretable-neuron shares, and no InceptionV1-sized vision-model estimates.
No attribution-graph test of whether model neurons explain behavior without a replacement model.
Tests automated explanation validation for GPT-2 feature models at Layer 9, not a broad audit of neuron poles or other models.
Reports F1 distributions for three feature methods, but not the proportion above a stated threshold for ‘good’ scores or comparisons across explainer-model strengths.

rows.subject: SAE trained on GPT-2 Small residual-stream pre-activations at Layer 9
rows.operation_detail: GPT-4o-generated feature explanation was scored by GPT-4o on held-out activating and non-activating examples; F1 measured against activation labels.

conditions.value: at least five new activating and five non-activating examples per feature

rows.uncertainty: not stated for this method’s F1 distribution
rows.note: The paper says SAE and LCA features have comparable interpretability, with median F1-scores around 0.6. Across methods, Kruskal-Wallis H = 1856.33, p < 0.001; Dunn’s tests with Bonferroni correction found SAE significantly below MLP (p < 0.001).
rows.check: Subject is an SAE dictionary feature, not a GPT-2 neuron. The F1 is binary detection on 5+5 held-out examples, not simulation scoring, and is used to compare encoders (the study's own method comparison). Figure 7 labels the mean as μ=0.63 and N=2500, while the text says 500 features; the reported median of about 0.6 comes from the text.

rows.uncertainty: not stated for this method’s F1 distribution
rows.note: The paper describes MLP scores as higher and their distribution as tighter than SAE and LCA scores. Dunn’s tests with Bonferroni correction found MLP significantly above SAE and LCA (p < 0.001).
rows.check: Subject is the study's own MLP-encoder dictionary feature, not a model neuron. This is the method comparison result, not a measure of neuron explanation quality. Figure 7 shows μ=0.83.
